Order rows using column values

Source: R/arrange.R
arrange.tbl_gpu.Rd

arrange() orders the rows of a GPU table by the values of the columns you name, as dplyr::arrange() does. The sort runs on the GPU.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
arrange(.data, ..., .by_group = FALSE, .locale = NULL)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Columns to sort by. A bare column, desc(column), pick() of columns, and -column of a numeric or logical column sort on the GPU. Any other expression, such as arrange(x + y) or -column of a factor, string or date column (where R's - warns or errors), is evaluated by dplyr on the CPU. The first key is the primary sort key, the second breaks its ties, and so on.

.by_group

If TRUE and .data is grouped, sort by the grouping columns first (ascending), then by .... Default is FALSE.

.locale

The locale to sort character vectors in. NULL (the default) and "C" sort by byte order on the GPU; any other locale is sorted by dplyr on the CPU (with stringi).

Value

A tbl_gpu with the rows reordered and the groups of .data. The sorted result is new GPU memory (about twice the table size at peak).

Details

Sort order

  • Ascending by default; desc(column) or -column sorts descending.

  • With several keys, the first is the primary key, the second breaks its ties, and so on.

  • The sort is stable: rows that tie keep their original order.

Missing values

NA and NaN sort last, in ascending and in descending order, as in dplyr.

Memory usage

The arrange operation requires approximately 2x the table size in GPU memory:

  • Original table

  • Sort indices (4 bytes per row)

  • New sorted table

For very large tables, consider filtering to reduce size before sorting.

Supported column types

Every column type a GPU table holds can be a sort key: double, integer, integer64, character, logical, factor, Date and POSIXct. A factor sorts by the order of its levels, as in dplyr.

Character columns sort by byte (UTF-8) order, which is dplyr's default "C" locale. Another .locale, or options(dplyr.legacy_locale = TRUE), sorts in dplyr on the CPU.

See also

filter.tbl_gpu for filtering rows, select.tbl_gpu for selecting columns, collect.tbl_gpu for retrieving results

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)

  # Sort by single column (ascending)
  sorted <- gpu_mtcars |>
    arrange(mpg) |>
    collect()

  # Sort descending
  sorted_desc <- gpu_mtcars |>
    arrange(desc(mpg)) |>
    collect()

  # Multiple columns: primary and secondary sort keys
  sorted_multi <- gpu_mtcars |>
    arrange(cyl, desc(mpg)) |>
    collect()

  # With grouped data
  grouped_sort <- gpu_mtcars |>
    group_by(cyl) |>
    arrange(mpg, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    collect()
}
